after: ## Structure of the Earth (6.1.1) and the continents (6.1.2)
alt: Cut-away of the Earth showing a thin rigid crust, a thick mantle of slowly moving hot rock and a very hot dense core of iron and nickel. Below, oceanic crust is drawn thinner and denser than continental crust.
caption: Crust, mantle and core: heat from the core drives movement in the mantle.

alt: Cross-section of an ocean plate moving over a fixed plume of hot mantle rock. An active volcano sits over the plume; extinct volcanoes further along the direction of plate movement get older and lower with distance. Below: how to describe a distribution with a pattern, named locations and the hotspot exception.
caption: Most volcanoes follow plate boundaries; hotspots are the exception.

alt: Top: convection currents in the mantle; hot rock rises, spreads, cools and sinks, dragging the plates above. Below, three boundaries: divergent, where plates move apart and magma forms new crust; convergent, where the denser oceanic plate is subducted and a line of volcanoes forms; conservative, where plates slide past and cause earthquakes only.
caption: Movement, process, hazard: subduction at convergent boundaries gives earthquakes and a line of volcanoes.

alt: Cross-section with the focus underground, seismic waves spreading out from it, and the epicentre on the surface directly above where shaking is strongest. Below, a magnitude 6.0, 7.0 and 8.0 earthquake are linked by steps of about 32 times more energy, so 8.0 releases about 1,000 times the energy of 6.0.
caption: The focus is underground, the epicentre above it; each magnitude step is about 32 times the energy.

alt: Cross-section of an erupting volcano: magma rises from underground and pours out as lava; an ash cloud rises above the crater; volcanic bombs are thrown out; a pyroclastic flow of hot gas, ash and rock rushes downslope; gases including sulfur dioxide drift away and fall as acid rain.
caption: Magma underground becomes lava at the surface; ash, gases, bombs and pyroclastic flows are the other features.

alt: Three columns on a timeline around the event. Before: monitoring and warning, land use zoning, the structure of buildings and disaster preparation. During: evacuation. After: rebuilding and international aid. Shelters span both during and after. Each card gives a benefit or limitation.
caption: Sort strategies into before, during and after, then weigh each one.

alt: A volcano landscape numbered 1 to 5: fields on fertile lower slopes, mineral deposits such as sulfur, a quarry for basalt, a geothermal power station using water heated by hot rock, and tourists at the crater. A key explains each opportunity.
caption: Fertile soils, minerals, building stone, geothermal power and tourism can outweigh the risk.
